payrollConfig.title: Payroll configuration
payrollConfig.description: Per-company payroll schedule and statutory employer identity.
payrollConfig.emptyScope: No companies in the current scope. Use the company switcher above.
payrollConfig.dayHint: Day of month (1–31). Leave blank for month-end. Scheduling reference only — it does not change how the pay period is calculated.
payrollConfig.hrdfHint: Registration numbers appear on statutory files and payslips.
payrollConfig.cutOffsHint: Day of month (1–31). Blank = month-end. The salary/inputs cut-off is set above as Cut-off day. These are the COMPANY DEFAULT cut-off windows: payroll pulls each transaction type (overtime, claims, unpaid leave, attendance) from its configured window when an employee's payroll policy doesn't set its own. Statutory contributions still aggregate per calendar month.
payrollConfig.defaultPolicyHint: Applied to every employee who has no payroll policy assigned individually.
payrollConfig.releaseHint: Controls when employees can see their payslip in self-service. Fixed day = a day of the month after the pay period; relative = days before(-)/after(+) pay day. Never before payroll closes.
payrollConfig.statutoryReadOnlyHint: Shown for reference only. These employer registration details are one record with one owner — Organization → Statutory. They used to be editable here as well, so whichever screen saved last silently won.
payrollConfig.movedSettingsHint: Probation length, review reminders and the default salary currency are not payroll settings and have moved:
payrollConfig.listDescription: Choose a company to view or change its payroll timing.

errors.invalidDefaultPolicy: The chosen default payroll policy must be an active policy in this company.

employeeIdConfig.title: Employee ID Auto Running Number Setup
employeeIdConfig.description: Define how new Employee IDs are generated — prefix, starting number, digits and scope.
employeeIdConfig.gapNotice: Employee IDs are guaranteed unique but not strictly gap-free: deleted employees, manually keyed IDs, or replacing a setup can leave gaps in the sequence.
employeeIdConfig.empty: No Employee ID setups yet. Create one to auto-generate Employee IDs at hire.
employeeIdConfig.deleteDescription: The "{prefix}" numbering setup will be removed. Existing employees keep their IDs.
employeeIdConfig.fieldScopeHint: Global shares one sequence across all companies; company-specific keeps a separate sequence per company.
employeeIdConfig.fieldPrefixHint: Letters, numbers and dashes. Prefix + digits + suffix together must be at most 30 characters.
employeeIdConfig.fieldCurrentHint: The last number issued. The next hire receives the following number.

errors.duplicateActive: An active Employee ID setup already exists for this scope
errors.prefixCollision: Another active setup already uses this prefix
errors.tooLong: Prefix, number length and suffix together must be at most 30 characters

employeeIdConfig.fieldTemplateNameHint: Optional label so several numbering formats can run side by side.
employeeIdConfig.fieldSuffixHint: Optional text after the number, e.g. MY → EMP0001MY. Letters, numbers and dashes.
employeeIdConfig.fieldLengthHint: Leading zeroes: the number is padded to this many digits.
employeeIdConfig.fieldAllowManualOverrideHint: When on, HR may hand-key an Employee ID (checked for uniqueness) instead of auto-generating it.
employeeIdConfig.cp39LengthNote: Note: Employee IDs longer than 10 characters do not fit the LHDN CP39 submission file — CP39 generation will list the affected employees instead of truncating. Longer IDs remain fully usable everywhere else.

payrollPolicy.title: Payroll policies
payrollPolicy.description: Named, reusable rules for how each employee's payroll is processed. Assign a policy to an employee and payroll applies it automatically.
payrollPolicy.previewNotice: General Settings below (proration, negative net pay, overtime caps, leave divisors, rounding) are live and applied during payroll calculation. Statutory minimums (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, and the EA 1955 overtime floor) always stay locked and cannot be set below the law. Custom-period cut-off windows are recorded but not yet applied to calculation.
payrollPolicy.typeDefaultHint: The policy type and payment frequency here are template defaults for new assignments. An existing employee's Pay Mode and Payment Term are set on their Basic Salary record (Personnel → Payroll tab).
payrollPolicy.emptyScope: No companies in the current scope. Use the company switcher above.
payrollPolicy.deleteDescription: Delete the policy "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
payrollPolicy.typeHint: Monthly and Daily are applied to payroll. A Daily policy pays its per-day rate for the eligible days worked in the period — monthly proration does not apply. Hourly is configurable now (rate plus shift-schedule setting) but its live payslip generation is a signed-off follow-up. Custom-period is configurable now (a cut-off window with an anchor day); applying that window to overtime, attendance and leave is a signed-off follow-up.
payrollPolicy.assignHint: Payroll uses the assigned policy automatically on the next run. Leave on the default for standard monthly processing.
payrollPolicy.assignInactiveNote: The assigned policy is inactive, so payroll falls back to the monthly default.

errors.duplicateName: A payroll policy with this name already exists for this company.
errors.inUse: This policy is assigned to employees and cannot be deleted. Unassign it first.
errors.companyMismatch: A payroll policy can only be assigned to employees in its own company.
errors.defaultInUse: This payroll policy is set as a company default and cannot be deleted.

payrollPolicy.dailyHint: Daily policies pay a per-day rate for the days worked in the period; monthly proration does not apply. The per-day rate is required for a Daily policy.
payrollPolicy.fieldOnlyWithinShift: Only pull hours within shift schedule
payrollPolicy.onlyWithinShiftHint: When on, only hours worked within the employee's assigned rostered shift are payable. Hours clocked outside the shift, overtime beyond the shift, and any day with no rostered shift are excluded. When off, all worked hours count.
payrollPolicy.hourlyHint: Hourly policies pay a per-hour rate for the hours worked in the period. The per-hour rate is required for an Hourly policy. Live end-to-end hourly payslip generation is a signed-off follow-up; today an Hourly policy stores its rate and shift-schedule setting and can be assigned, but is not yet applied to a payroll run.
payrollPolicy.customPeriodHint: Custom-period policies record a cut-off window — an anchor day for a non-calendar pay period. Choose "Custom period" and set the anchor day to store the window. The window is saved and validated now, but is not yet applied to a payroll run (applying it to overtime, attendance and leave is a signed-off follow-up). Statutory months (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB) always stay on the calendar month by law and are never moved by the window.

cutOff.title: Cut-off window
cutOff.anchorDayHint: Used only for the "Custom period" mode. The anchor day (1–28) is the day of the month the window opens — for example, anchor 25 means the window runs from the 25th of the previous month to the 24th of the period month. Applies only to Custom-period policies; statutory months stay on the calendar month.
cutOff.frequencyHint: How often payroll runs. Weekly and bi-weekly are operational cadences — statutory contributions (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB) are still aggregated and reported per calendar month, as required by law.
cutOff.perTypeHint: Each transaction type can close on its own anchor day (1–28). Leave blank to inherit the salary anchor day above. Only used when the period mode is "Custom period".
cutOff.previewHint: The dates each transaction type will be picked up for the current month, derived from the saved cut-off configuration. Consecutive periods are contiguous and never overlap.
cutOff.perFrequencyHint: When the payroll frequency is Weekly or Bi-Weekly, that frequency can use its own anchor day and per-type cut-off days. Leave blank to inherit the Monthly (base) cut-off above. Only used when the period mode is "Custom period".
cutOff.scheduleHint: The cut-off cycles this payroll frequency generates for the month. Weekly and bi-weekly split the month into contiguous cycles; statutory contributions are still aggregated per calendar month by law.

config.salaryIncrementProration: Split a mid-month salary increment across the two rates
config.prorationHint: Used when a joiner/leaver works part of the month. Default (calendar days) reproduces today's figures.
config.salaryConfigHint: Configure the basic-salary formula for each employee event independently. Leaving an event at "default" inherits the basis above.
config.incrementHint: When on, a mid-month pay raise is split day-by-day across the old and new rate.
config.negativeCarryForward: Carry the balance forward to the next cycle
config.negativeNetHint: "Carry forward" holds this cycle's net at zero and recovers the shortfall from the next cycle's net pay.
config.otExceedConvert: Convert the excess to a pay item
config.otHint: The multiplier is floored at the statutory 1.5×. Convert redirects any overtime above the cap onto the chosen pay item so it is still paid.
config.deductAbsentDaysHint: A scheduled working day with no attendance record, or one marked Absent, is deducted at the same daily rate as unpaid leave, before EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB. Approved leave, public holidays and rest days are never counted, and the roster wins over the company calendar. Off by default; it applies only to payroll runs made after it is turned on.
config.leaveHint: Divisors decide how one unpaid day / encashed day is valued. Default (calendar month) reproduces today's figures.
config.roundingHint: Statutory contribution rounding always follows its own legislated rules and is unaffected.

wizard.requiredHint: Complete the required fields on this step to continue.
wizard.reviewHint: Review the configuration below, then Save. Use Previous to return to any step and amend.
wizard.reviewDraftNote: Saved as a draft, this policy is not applied to payroll. Activate it from the policy list when ready.

validation.dailyRate: Enter a per-day rate greater than zero.
validation.hourlyRate: Enter a per-hour rate greater than zero.

leaveApproval.description: Choose who signs off on leave, and in what order, for each company.
leaveApproval.empty: No steps yet — add at least one.
leaveApproval.archiveConfirm: Delete this rule? Requests already in progress keep their current approval chain.
leaveApproval.noRules: No scoped rules yet. All requests use the default chain above.
leaveApproval.templatesHint: Reusable approval chains you build once and assign to many leave types and companies.
leaveApproval.templateSaveFailed: This template could not be saved. Try again, or ask your administrator.
leaveApproval.discardBody: You changed this template and have not saved it.
leaveApproval.deleteTemplateConfirm: Delete this template? It must not be assigned anywhere first.
leaveApproval.tenantDefaultHint: Applies automatically to every company and leave type with no specific rule.
leaveApproval.assignmentsHint: Map a template to many leave types and companies in one step.
leaveApproval.noTemplates: No templates yet — add one to reuse it across leave types.
leaveApproval.unassignConfirm: Remove this assignment? The leave type falls back to the default chain.
leaveApproval.rolesGatedNote: Steps route as follows: Direct manager goes to the employee's recorded direct superior; Manager's Manager goes one level above that; Department Head / Business Unit Head go to the head set for that unit in the Head (leave approver) column under Settings → System Labels; HR and HR Manager go to HR admins; Payroll goes to payroll partners; Custom Role goes to an HR admin. A step is skipped when nobody fills its role — no direct superior recorded, or no head set for that unit. An HR admin can also clear any step, so a chain always completes.
leaveApproval.workflowsHint: Every configured approval workflow. Open one to see or change its steps and conditions.
leaveApproval.noWorkflows: No workflows configured yet. Requests use the company default chain.
leaveApproval.workflowTypeAutoHint: Approvers follow the employee's reporting line automatically — no level-by-level setup needed.
leaveApproval.advancedOverrideHint: Use a template or build a custom approval chain that diverges from the reporting line.
leaveApproval.workflowTypeDefaultHint: Use a ready-made template. No level-by-level setup needed.
leaveApproval.noActiveTemplates: No active templates yet — create one above first.
leaveApproval.saveConfirmBody: Are you sure you want to save this approval workflow configuration?
leaveApproval.escalationHint: Chase a leave request that has sat with an approver for too long.
leaveApproval.escalationNotifyNote: Escalation alerts are delivered to the notification bell.
leaveApproval.templateCreationHint: Build a reusable approval flow and its steps here.
leaveApproval.multiStepNote: A template with two or more steps is a multi-step approval; a one-step template is a single approver. The template you assign decides — there is no separate company switch.
leaveApproval.assignmentTemplateHint: Decide which companies, leave types and employees each approval flow applies to.
leaveApproval.noEligibilityRules: No eligibility rules for the chosen companies.
leaveApproval.ruleNotAssignable: This rule narrows by something an approval flow cannot scope on. Use a rule based on company, employment type and grade group.
leaveApproval.legacyGradeScope: Assigned by grade — re-assign by eligibility rule
leaveApproval.escalationSectionHint: Chase an approval that has stalled. Set per company — open the one you need.
leaveApproval.fixedWarning: A fixed approver cannot be skipped. If this person leaves, requests stop at this level until the template is edited.
leaveApproval.hintDirectManager: Resolved from the employee's reporting line when the request is made. Skipped if no direct superior is recorded.
leaveApproval.hintDepartmentHead: Resolved from the employee's department. Skipped if that department has no head set.
leaveApproval.hintBusinessUnitHead: Resolved from the employee's business unit. Skipped if that business unit has no head set.
leaveApproval.hintHr: Goes to HR admins. Never skipped.
leaveApproval.hintHrManager: Goes to HR admins. Never skipped.
leaveApproval.hintPayroll: Goes to payroll partners for the employee's company. Never skipped.
leaveApproval.hintCustomRole: Goes to an HR admin. Never skipped.
leaveApproval.previewHint: Pick an employee and a leave type to see the exact chain their request would take against today's org chart.
leaveApproval.previewIdle: Choose an employee to preview their approval chain.
leaveApproval.previewNoResult: No approval chain could be resolved for this employee.
leaveApproval.previewSkippedNoManager: Skipped — no direct superior is recorded for this employee.
leaveApproval.previewSkippedNoDepartmentHead: Skipped — this employee's department has no head set.
leaveApproval.previewSkippedNoBusinessUnitHead: Skipped — this employee's business unit has no head set.
leaveApproval.previewSourceFallback: From the built-in chain (no rule or default matches)
leaveApproval.previewSingleApprover: One level — this is a single-approver request, not a chain.
leaveApproval.previewAllDropped: Every level was skipped — this request is approved with no approval step.
leaveApproval.previewSearchPlaceholder: Search by Employee ID or name
leaveApproval.hintManagerManager: Resolved from the employee's reporting line, one level above their direct manager. Skipped if either level is missing.
leaveApproval.previewSkippedNoManagerManager: Skipped — no manager's manager is recorded for this employee.
leaveApproval.hintSpecificEmployee: Always this person, whoever they report to. This level is never skipped — if they leave, requests stop here until the template is edited.
leaveApproval.fixedApproverEnded: This person is no longer an active employee. Requests will stop at this level until you choose someone else.
leaveApproval.fixedApproverMissing: Choose the person who approves at this level.
leaveApproval.previewFixedApproverEnded: This approver is no longer an active employee — requests stop here.
leaveApproval.modeSequentialHint: Each level has one approver, and must approve before the next level becomes active.
leaveApproval.modeAnyOneHint: A level can list several approvers, and any one of them can approve for that level.
leaveApproval.addAlternate: Add another approver for this level
leaveApproval.previewAnyOne: Any one of these can approve

taxRelief.title: Tax Relief (Form TP1)
taxRelief.intro: Submit monthly TP1 relief and follow its approval. Only approved relief feeds payroll.
taxRelief.amountHelp: Enter the total optional reliefs you intend to claim for the year — for example life insurance, medical, lifestyle, and education fees. This is a single annual amount.
taxRelief.submittedNotice: A submitted declaration needs employer approval before it affects payroll. A correction keeps the earlier record.
taxRelief.historicalDraft: Saved as a draft for this assessment year.
taxRelief.historicalNone: No declaration was made for this assessment year.
taxRelief.historyNote: Previous submissions are kept and visible in your record history. Past assessment years are shown read-only.
taxRelief.totalNote: Your annual total is calculated automatically from the categories above when you save or submit.
taxRelief.remarksPlaceholder: Any notes or declaration for HR (optional).

individual.label: Individual and dependent relatives (RM)
individual.help: Standard individual relief and dependent relatives. Statutory cap RM 9,000.

spouse.label: Spouse / alimony (RM)
spouse.help: Relief for a non-working spouse or alimony payments. Statutory cap RM 4,000.

children.label: Children (RM)
children.help: Total qualifying-child relief for the year.

parent.label: Parents (RM)
parent.help: Medical, care or examination expenses for your parents.

medicalInsurance.label: Medical / insurance (RM)
medicalInsurance.help: Life and medical insurance, EPF, and approved medical expenses.

lifestyle.label: Lifestyle (RM)
lifestyle.help: Books, computers, sports equipment, internet and similar lifestyle expenses.

education.label: Education fees (RM)
education.help: Approved course or tuition fees for yourself.

other.label: Other reliefs (RM)
other.help: Any other TP1 relief category not listed above.

taxRelief.sectionCHelp: Enter what you are claiming now. The annual limit and what has already been approved this year are shown against each item; if you key more than is left, the box is reduced to what remains and the reason is shown beside it.

limit.lineLimit: {label}: the amount keyed ({claim}) is more than the limit this line is printed with on the form ({limit}). Please reduce it.
limit.itemLimit: {label}: the total keyed for this item ({claim}) is more than its annual limit ({limit}). Please reduce it.
limit.annualRemaining: {label}: this claim takes the assessment year {over} past the annual limit of {limit}. {already} has already been approved for this year, so at most {remaining} can be claimed now.
limit.clampedLine: {label}: annual limit {limit}, {already} already approved this assessment year, {remaining} still available. More than that was keyed, so the amount has been reduced to {remaining}.
limit.clampedItem: {label}: annual limit {limit}, {already} already approved this assessment year. The other lines keyed on this item leave {remaining} for this box, so the amount has been reduced to {remaining}.

taxRelief.countedNote: Every OTHER approved declaration for this assessment year — the one on this form is left out, so a correction is never refused by the figure it replaces. This is the year's total, not the amount used for any single month: payroll takes only what is effective by the month it is running.
taxRelief.countedNone: Nothing else has been approved for this assessment year yet.
taxRelief.countedUnattributedNote: {amount} of this was declared before the full TP1 form existed. It is included in the amount sent to the tax calculation, but it cannot be shown against a numbered item, so it is not part of the Remaining figures below.
taxRelief.legacyNote: This declaration was recorded before the full TP1 form was available. It is shown as it was entered, and it still feeds your monthly tax deduction.
taxRelief.rebateNote: A rebate reduces the tax itself, not the income it is calculated on, so it is not part of the total above.
taxRelief.declarationText: I acknowledge that all the information stated in this form is true, correct, and complete. If the information provided is found to be false, legal action may be taken against me under paragraph 113(1)(b) of the Income Tax Act 1967.
taxRelief.consentIntro: Approve this claim for a deduction month, or refuse it.

tp3.title: Form TP3 — previous employment
tp3.intro: The previous employment's figures for an employee who joined part-way through the year, laid out in the official form's own sections so a paper TP3 can be worked down in order. Stage 1: this record is captured and printed. It changes no tax — the monthly PCB still reads the four opening-balance figures on the employee's Payroll tab.
tp3.stageNote: Both sections now reach the monthly tax deduction. Saving this form writes Section C's remuneration, EPF, PCB and zakat, and Section D's total reliefs, into the figures the payroll run reads.

tp3.reconcileHeading: Against the figures the tax calculation uses
tp3.reconcileNote: The monthly PCB reads five opening-balance figures for this employee. Saving this form writes all five from the boxes above — gross less the exempt allowances less EPF, the EPF itself, the PCB already deducted, the zakat, and the total of the Section D reliefs. They are shown here so you can see what the tax calculation will use; a difference on the first four means someone edited them by hand on the Payroll tab afterwards.
tp3.reconcileNoStored: No opening balances are recorded for this year on the employee's Payroll tab.
tp3.reconcileStoredOtherYear: The opening balances on the employee's Payroll tab are recorded against {year}, not this year.
tp3.selectEmployeePrompt: Choose an employee to open their Form TP3.
tp3.noRecordYet: No Form TP3 has been recorded for this employee for {year}.

tp3.exemptLimitNote: The exemption limits below come from LHDN's monthly tax deduction specification, not from the TP3 form — the form prints no limit column in this section. Whatever you key is recorded exactly as it is and is never trimmed. An amount above a limit stays taxable, so only the part up to the limit counts towards Accumulated Net Remuneration.
tp3.exemptOverLimit: Above the RM {limit} exemption limit by RM {excess}. The excess is taxable, and it is added to Accumulated Net Remuneration below.

tp3.totalEpfCounted: [retired r348 — replaced by totalGross / totalLessExempt / totalLessEpf / totalExcessNote]
tp3.totalCappedNote: [retired r348 — replaced by totalGross / totalLessExempt / totalLessEpf / totalExcessNote]
tp3.totalLessExempt: [retired r350 — replaced by totalPlusExcess / totalExemptNote; C1 holds only taxable pay, so the C2 excess is ADDED, not subtracted]
tp3.totalExcessNote: [retired r350 — replaced by totalPlusExcess / totalExemptNote; C1 holds only taxable pay, so the C2 excess is ADDED, not subtracted]
tp3.totalExemptNote: Of the RM {entered} keyed across the C2 boxes, RM {exempt} is within the statutory exemption limits and is not taxed. C1 carries only taxable pay, so the exempt amount is never deducted from it — only the RM {excess} above the limits is added.
tp3.totalNoLimitNote: No annual exemption limit is published for C2(iii) or C2(v), so no part of those boxes can be shown to be taxable and nothing from them is added.

anomaly.subtitle: Everything in this run that needs a human decision, worst first.

Verdicts below reflect that placeholder, not a rule tuned to this company. A defensible threshold comes from this company’s own pay history or a parallel run.

action.negativeNet: Review the deductions — take-home pay cannot be negative.

action.prorationMismatch: Check the hire and termination dates against the days paid.
action.prorationMismatchFull: A full period was paid, but this person joined or left partway through. Check the dates.
action.duplicateEmploymentPay: The same person is paid under more than one employment this period. Confirm that is intended.
action.netSwing: Check what changed for this person this cycle.
action.componentAppeared: Confirm this new pay item is correct.
action.componentVanished: Confirm this pay item was meant to stop.
action.hypothesisMissedIncrement: Colleagues on this run moved up and this person did not. Check whether an increment or an adjustment was missed.
action.hypothesisOutOfStepWithPeers: This person’s pay moved in a way the rest of the run did not. Check what changed for them.
action.hypothesisComponentDrift: Overtime or allowance is a very different share of this person’s pay than their colleagues’. Check the underlying entries.
action.hypothesisDeductionOutlier: Deductions take a very different share of this person’s pay than their colleagues’. Check the recurring deductions on the record.
action.hypothesisStatutoryCategoryDoubt: Statutory contributions are a very different share of this person’s pay than their colleagues’. Check the contribution category on the record.

controlTower.howDescription: What runs, in what order, which parts use AI, and what is switched on right now.
controlTower.loopIntro: Every cycle runs the same five steps. Only one of them involves AI, and none of them decides anything on its own.
controlTower.loopAlt: Five steps: checks run, findings are recorded, AI explains them in plain words, a person decides, and the result feeds back.
controlTower.step2Sub: with the figures that caused them
controlTower.step3Sub: AI writes it in plain words
controlTower.step4Sub: accept, fix, or approve what the AI proposes closing
controlTower.step5Sub: measures how well it is doing
controlTower.loopBack: What people decide is what tells us whether the checks are set right.
controlTower.agentsIntro: Read live from your own setup, not from a list someone wrote. If something says it is off, the reason is next to it.

agent.detectorsDoes: Looks at every employee in a finished payroll run and decides whether it is clear, needs a look, or must be blocked. No AI is involved and the answer never varies for the same figures.
agent.sweepDoes: Runs the checks every night at 02:30 so the queue is already filled when you open it, instead of waiting for someone to press a button.
agent.narratorDoes: Turns a finding into a sentence you can read. It can only use the figures already recorded — if it produces a number those figures do not support, the sentence is thrown away rather than shown.
agent.assistantDoes: Answers employees’ questions about their own records — leave, pay, and why their pay changed — so they do not have to ask a person.
agent.autonomyDoes: Clearing or changing anything without a person. Nothing in this system does this today.
agent.actionsDoes: Finds exceptions that were raised because something was missing from an employee record — and that record now has it. It proposes closing them; you approve, and each one is checked again as you do. It never changes an employee record.
agent.hypothesesDoes: AI drafting is not used in scheduled runs. The scheduled principal is not admitted to model spending; a configured provider does not enable it.
agent.nudgeDoes: Notices whose record is missing something payroll needs, and tells the one person who can fix it — the employee for their own bank details, HR for everything only HR can key in. It sends nothing until you switch it on.
agent.payRuleDrafterDoes: Turns a sentence like “RM5 for every hour worked” into one of a fixed set of pay rules, which is then checked by the same code the payroll engine uses. It never saves anything — you review it and press save.
agent.reportDesignerDoes: Turns a description of a report into a draft layout, checked against the same rules the report builder enforces. It sees the shape of your data, never the data.
agent.reviewDrafterDoes: Drafts the wording of a manager’s performance review from what has already been recorded. The manager edits it and owns it; nothing is saved on their behalf.
agent.planDrafterDoes: Drafts a reply to an improvement request raised from inside the product. This is our own tooling rather than a feature of your plan.
agent.triageDoes: AI drafting is not used in scheduled runs. The scheduled principal is not admitted to model spending; a configured provider does not enable it.
agent.onehrEvidenceDrafterDoes: Selects and orders authorized evidence passages for a human to edit. Deterministic checks resolve every passage; it cannot invent claims or make assessment or pay decisions.

why.actionsOn: Suggestions appear on Proposed actions. Nothing is closed until you approve it.
why.hypothesesOn: Running every night on the people the fixed checks cleared. Anything it raises is for review only and never blocks a payroll run.
why.hypothesesOff: Not switched on. The fixed checks still run; this is the extra look that compares each person with their colleagues, and it stays off until you ask for it.
why.nudgeOn: Switched on. Reminders go out on the nightly run.
why.scheduledModelNotAdmitted: AI drafting is not used in scheduled runs. The scheduled principal is not admitted to model spending; a configured provider does not enable it.
why.nudgeTemplates: Scheduled reminders use fixed templates. AI drafting is not used.
why.scheduledUnattributed: An administrator must switch this on again to attribute scheduled work.
why.nudgeOff: Not switched on. Nobody is contacted automatically until you ask for it.

why.planDrafterOff: Deliberately off. This is Stradaverse’s own tooling, not part of your plan.
why.triageOn: Reading new claims every night and asking the person who filed them. Nothing it asks can refuse or change a claim.
why.triageOff: Not switched on. Claims are read by people only, and nobody is asked anything automatically.

controlTower.domainsIntro: Payroll is the first area. The same machinery is built to cover the others, and they are listed here so you can see what is coming rather than assuming payroll is all there is.

domain.payrollDoes: Checks every finished payroll run for figures that look wrong, missing bank or tax details, and pay without attendance.
domain.readinessDoes: Would check every employee record all the time, not just at payroll, so a missing bank account is found and fixed long before it blocks anyone’s pay.
domain.onboardingDoes: Would check that a new joiner’s record is complete and correct before their first payroll, instead of finding out during it.
domain.complianceDoes: Would watch for changes to contribution rates and forms, and prepare the update for you to approve.

controlTower.promisesTitle: Two things this will not do
controlTower.promise1: AI never works out your pay.
controlTower.promise1Body: Every figure — salary, tax, contributions, overtime — is calculated by the payroll engine, the same way every time, and tested against known answers. AI is only ever used to describe a figure that has already been calculated. It cannot change one.
controlTower.promise2: AI never decides anything on its own.
controlTower.promise2Body: Whether something is cleared, flagged or blocked is decided by fixed rules before any AI is involved, and the explanation cannot change that decision. Nothing is cleared, paid or altered without a person.

actions.description: Work the AI would like to take off your desk. Nothing here happens until you approve it, and you can see exactly why each one is being proposed.
actions.emptyBody: Every payroll exception still waiting on you has a real problem behind it. When somebody fixes the underlying record, the exception will appear here to be closed.
actions.staleNote: The other {stale} were left open. They were checked again as you approved, and no longer qualified — either the problem has come back, or somebody had already dealt with them.
actions.reversibleNote: This only records a decision about the exception. It changes no pay, no rate and no employee record, and checking the payroll run again replaces it.
actions.recheckNote: Each one is checked again the moment you press this. Anything that has gone wrong again since the page loaded is left open.
actions.overCap: One approval closes at most {cap}, and there are {total}. Approve these, then come back for the rest.

controlTower.howAiTitle: The AI pieces and where to manage them
controlTower.howAiBody: Besides this checking loop, the system has an HR assistant with a capability for each HR module, three scheduled agents, and AI built into other screens. AI management shows each one, whether it can run, and where to change it.

profileRequestSettings.title: Employee Change Requests
profileRequestSettings.description: Control what employees can see and change in My Profile, photo editing and who approves requests.
profileRequestSettings.readOnlyNotice: You can see this configuration but not change it — only a group administrator can.
profileRequestSettings.approverHelp: One person decides each request, and nobody can ever decide their own. Both choices are administrators because approving writes the master record, and only an administrator may write it — see the note below.

approverOptionHelp.admin: Including an administrator whose access covers one company. This is how the system behaves today if you change nothing.
approverOptionHelp.group_admin: A super administrator, or an HR administrator whose access covers the whole group. An administrator for a single company can no longer sign these off.

profileRequestSettings.singleLevelNote: A request is settled by one decision. There is no second level of approval, and a manager cannot be made the approver — approving writes the employee record itself, which only an administrator is permitted to do.
profileRequestSettings.unknownApprover: That is not one of the approver options.
profileRequestSettings.fieldsHelp: Choose one permission per field: Editable allows permitted changes; View Only shows the value without editing; Hide removes it from My Profile. Some changes still need HR approval. Use the column controls to apply a permission to all applicable fields.
profileRequestSettings.lockWithdrawsNotice: Changing an editable field to View Only or Hide rejects pending requests containing that field. Employees see the reason; their records are not updated and request history is kept.
profileRequestSettings.withdrawnReason: This field is no longer open to change requests. Please contact HR if it still needs correcting.

config.checklistHint: A requisition checklist is the common list plus the company list. A key stays the same when you rename an item.

config.fieldsHint: Extra staff-only fields on cases. They are never shown to the new hire. Leave companies empty to apply to all.
config.catalogueHint: What an employee may request, and how many approval levels each item needs. An inactive item is hidden from requesters.

rewards.seniorMembershipHelp: Choose individual employees for the Senior Plan. Members are excluded from standard bonus and lump-sum awards; salary-increase eligibility is assessed separately.
rewards.seniorLegacyHelp: This review keeps its saved grade rule until you explicitly preview and adopt named membership. Historical reviews stay unchanged.
rewards.adoptNamedMembership: Convert this draft to named employee membership
rewards.searchSeniorMembership: Search by employee name or ID
rewards.noSeniorMembershipChanges: No individual membership changes. Confirming a legacy conversion still adopts named membership for this draft.
rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.description: Review salary increases and bonuses against separate budgets, then route approved awards to payroll.
rewards.empty: No reward reviews are available in your company scope. An administrator can create a cycle and assign your review role.
rewards.createHelp: Employees are read from their business-unit assignment and salary records on the snapshot date. Group Rewards must verify classifications and ratings before the BU CEO submits the review. No salaries change when you create a review.
rewards.privacyNote: Your own reward and restricted employee records are not listed. Unverified classifications are visible only to Group Rewards. Standard and JG H unit totals include restricted BG direct reports; EC direct reports use a separate plan.
rewards.matrixHelp: The same merit matrix applies to the standard and JG H plans. Values are percentages of monthly basic salary.
rewards.lumpHelp: One suggested amount per BU, funded from the remaining bonus balance. The lower amount across the standard and JG H plans applies to both. Individual changes require exception review. Zero means withheld.
rewards.noPeople: No employees match this view. Group Rewards must verify the roster before other reviewers can see it.
rewards.noChecks: No blocking checks or exceptions in this review.
rewards.route: BU CEO → BG CEO → Group Rewards → CTRO → Executive Chairman → Payroll
rewards.decisionReason: Decision note (required for returns, warnings and exceptions)
rewards.postHelp: The assigned payroll reviewer must also have company administrator access. Posting creates salary records and adds bonus awards to the selected draft payroll batch. It preserves existing overtime, deductions and bonus inputs. A posted review cannot be posted twice.
rewards.salaryOnly: Salary changes only, no bonus awards
rewards.accessHelp: Assign named users to every approval stage and payroll. Consecutive approval stages need different reviewers. A role applies only to this business unit and cycle. PBP is read-only.
rewards.locked: This review is locked. Return it to draft before changing its inputs.
rewards.dataHelp: Salary, employment and business-unit records come from Personnel. The CSV template contains only employees you may review. Use it to map talent and performance ratings, classify confidential reports and record case decisions. No employee or salary master records are imported from this template.
rewards.refreshHelp: Refresh the original snapshot date from Personnel. This clears input verification and requires another review. If an employee left the roster, the refresh is refused rather than silently deleting an award.

confidentialityFloor.bg: Marked BG confidential automatically: reports directly to the BG CEO seat holder in People. It can be made stricter, not lower.
confidentialityFloor.ec: Marked EC confidential automatically: reports directly to the Executive Chairman seat holder in People. It cannot be lowered.

sourceRefresh.title: Refresh source records
sourceRefresh.help: Current snapshot date: {date}. Preview what changed in People and Compensation since then before anything is changed.
sourceRefresh.willChange: What will change if you refresh to {date}

category.left: Left or moved out (kept on the list, marked, no increase or bonus)

sourceRefresh.confirmHelp: Open a row to see the names. Confirming moves the snapshot date to this date and clears data verification for the people who changed.

left.terminated: Left the company on {date}. Kept for the record; no increase or bonus.
left.moved: Moved out of this unit on {date}. Kept for the record; no increase or bonus.

sourceRefresh.eligibilityDates: Joined before {joinedBefore} · Confirmed by {confirmedBy} · Salary effective date {effectiveFrom}
sourceRefresh.eligibilityShared: The dates in the shared configuration {name}. You can review them in the review settings after creating it.

rewards.rulePools: Standard and JG H merit, promotion and special-adjustment pools are funded separately. No pool, plan or business unit may fund another. Nil-recommended eligible payroll remains in the pool base.
rewards.ruleBonus: Bonus utilisation equals standard bonus plus individual increases, less individual reductions, plus lump sums. Spending above 100% blocks approval, including positive spending against a zero budget. Less than 80% utilisation raises a warning.
rewards.ruleEC: EC direct reports have their own discretionary plan. Only Group Rewards, CTRO and Executive Chairman may see their line items. The 7% salary reference is advisory and does not block.
rewards.ruleExemption: A documented BU exemption lifts budget caps only. Eligibility, individual review thresholds and the approval route still apply.
rewards.ruleLump: Lump-sum tokens apply outside the standard bonus run, excluding ER cases, senior leadership and EC direct reports. The default suggestion uses the full remaining balance, rounded down in RM 50 steps. Group Rewards may configure the balance share, optional cap and rounding.
rewards.rulePrivacy: A user cannot view their own reward. BU CEOs cannot view BG CEO direct reports. The prototype’s inclusion of BG direct reports in unit totals is preserved; those totals may permit inference for small groups.
rewards.ruleApproval: Every unit follows the named approval route. Any change requires a return to draft and invalidates previous approvals. All checks are calculated on the full roster, including records hidden from the reviewer.
rewards.rulePosting: Rewards never calculates statutory deductions. Approved awards enter the existing salary and payroll services. Salary snapshots are checked again at posting; a failed employee or payroll write rolls back the whole unit.
rewards.configurationHelp: Group Rewards owns the policy for this review. Defaults reflect the supplied Reward Desk handover. Confirm them before submission. Changes require the review to be in draft.
rewards.rangesHelp: Salary ranges: grade, minimum RM, midpoint RM, maximum RM (one grade per line)
rewards.bonusMatrixHelp: Bonus matrix: grade, UA, BE, ME, AE, OU months (one grade per line)
rewards.branchFactorsHelp: Branch factors: segment, UA, BE, ME, AE, OU (one segment per line)
rewards.branchRatingsHelp: Branch ratings: branch, rating (UA / BE / ME / AE / OU)
rewards.lumpPolicyHelp: The handover uses 100% of the balance without a per-person cap. These are configurable policy defaults, not mandatory limits.
rewards.overrideHelp: Leave an amount blank to use the calculated recommendation. Enter zero to withhold an eligible award. Changes are saved together and checked against the unit budgets.
rewards.businessCase: Remarks / promotion business case (minimum 30 characters for promotion)
rewards.classificationHelp: Verify these reward inputs against approved performance and personnel records. Confidentiality must be correct before marking the row verified. Salary and employment dates remain owned by Personnel.
rewards.caseReason: BU CEO / PBP case decision and reason
rewards.unavailableHelp: Your role may not cover this review, or the service could not load it. Check your assigned Reward Desk access or try again.
rewards.offcycleFundingHelp: The monthly increase uses the unreserved remainder of the posted annual increment budget. Standard and JG H funds remain separate. Returned, rejected and withdrawn requests release their reservation.
rewards.exceptionHelp: Available only for an individual ad-hoc request. Explain the exception in at least 30 characters; EC approval is then required.
rewards.roleSummaryHelp: Save only the relevant role-change summaries below. Comparison extracts changed statements; it does not judge whether a promotion is justified. Each approver must review the summaries.
rewards.roleAcknowledgement: I have reviewed the current and proposed role summaries for the promotion requests visible to me.
rewards.roleComparisonHelp: Read current and proposed job descriptions locally, then review the extracted changes. Files and pasted source text are not uploaded or saved. PDF files must have a text layer and at most 10 pages. Files may be up to 5 MB; text up to 30,000 characters.

allowanceV2.description: Configure attendance-linked fixed earnings and deductions, then review their eligible periods before Payroll transfer.

allowanceV2.name: Name
allowanceV2.chooseCode: Choose a compatible fixed pay code
allowanceV2.archiveWarning: Archive this policy? Historical calculations and Payroll sources will remain available.
allowanceV2.setupDescription: Complete the four sections and review the rules before saving. Saving a policy does not transfer money.
allowanceV2.legacyNotice: This policy retains its original monthly criteria and employee scope. Existing results remain unchanged until an authorised recalculation.
allowanceV2.convertLegacy: Explicitly replace the legacy criteria with the new employee and attendance rules below. Review all conditions before saving.
allowanceV2.legacyScope: Existing company, department and business-unit scope is retained. Convert the policy to change employee selection.
allowanceV2.fixedRule: The fixed amount applies once per qualifying period. There is no automatic proration. Empty attendance criteria include applicable recorded days and scheduled absences; add an attendance-days condition when presence is required.
allowanceV2.weeklyRule: A week runs Monday through Sunday and belongs to the payment month containing its Sunday. A week spanning two months is counted once. A period starting before the policy effective date is excluded in full.

selectionModes.all: All employees in the policy company

allowanceV2.or: OR · at least one condition must pass
allowanceV2.employeeRule: An employee must match the employee selection AND satisfy the separate attendance conditions. Placement is resolved on the period’s last owned employment day; grade and category use the current Personnel values.
allowanceV2.allDaysHint: No selections means all supported day types.
allowanceV2.allShiftsHint: No selections means all shifts. Hold Ctrl or Command to select multiple options.
allowanceV2.measurementsHint: Recorded attendance owns measured time. Incomplete clockings and unknown required measurements do not qualify. Missing past scheduled days count as absences unless covered by approved leave; unrecorded rest, off and holiday dates do not earn an amount.
allowanceV2.reviewWarning: Saving creates a new policy version. Past policy versions, calculations and Payroll history are retained. Overlapping policies can add together when they share a pay code; review the preview for each policy before transfer.
allowanceV2.reviewConfirm: I reviewed the fixed amount, payment-period ownership, Payroll mapping and both sets of eligibility conditions.

attendanceWorkflow.title: Approval Workflow
attendanceWorkflow.subtitle: Configure independent approval templates for Attendance Irregularity and Self Overtime.
attendanceWorkflow.name: Workflow name
attendanceWorkflow.assignmentHelp: Values within one field are alternatives. Every filled field must match; empty fields include all eligible values in this company. Lower priority numbers apply first; ties are refused.
attendanceWorkflow.supportedApprovers: Attendance supports the direct administrative manager and HR administrators, including any-one alternatives and valid scoped delegation. The assigned manager is saved when submitted. If reporting authority later changes, HR can decide on behalf; personnel access is never expanded by routing.
attendanceWorkflow.anyOne: Any one of the manager or HR administrators may decide this stage
attendanceWorkflow.activationHelp: Activation validates the current employee population, reporting lines and overlapping assignments. Existing applications retain their saved stages. Routing is enabled separately for each company and application type.
attendanceWorkflow.previewTruncated: Showing the first 100 matching employees. Submission validates the actual employee again.
attendanceWorkflow.newVersionHelp: Saving creates a new version. Submitted applications and decisions keep their original version.
attendanceWorkflow.routingHelp: Until explicitly enabled, new applications use existing approval rules. Once enabled, a missing or ambiguous template blocks submission. Disabling affects new submissions only.
attendanceWorkflow.empty: No attendance approval workflows have been configured.
attendanceWorkflow.alternativeHelp: Any-one stages keep their usable alternatives. An unavailable manager or a self-only HR group is excluded from the saved routing; a stage with no active non-self approver blocks activation and submission.
attendanceWorkflow.companyHelp: Choose a company to manage its approval workflows.
attendanceWorkflow.orderedHelp: Levels proceed in order. Any eligible alternative can complete its current level; later levels must wait.
attendanceWorkflow.requestFailed: The request could not be completed. Your changes are kept; please try again.
attendanceWorkflow.legacyLevelsHelp: This workflow keeps its existing flat routing until you explicitly convert it. Pending applications keep their assigned approvers.
attendanceWorkflow.convertHierarchy: Use sequential hierarchy for new submissions
attendanceWorkflow.hierarchyLevelsHelp: Each Direct Superior level follows the preceding superior. Missing or invalid required approvers block submission unless this level explicitly offers HR as an alternative.

v3.sequentialHelp: Every selected person must approve in the displayed order.
v3.anyOneHelp: The first authorized decision completes this level.
v3.depthHelp: Depth is measured from the applicant, independently of the other approval levels.
v3.hrAlternative: Offer an explicit HR alternative for this superior level
v3.selectedHelp: Keep each selected employee required. To replace someone later, HR must record a reasoned change to that outstanding slot.
v3.summary: Check the approval levels below. Your draft is retained.
v3.levelHelp: Choose a mode and source independently for each level. Named employees are listed in their approval order.
v3.limits: One to ten levels; up to twenty named employees per level and one hundred participants per workflow.
v3.selectionRequired: Select at least one employee for this level.
v3.participantLimit: Use at most twenty participants per level and one hundred per workflow.
v3.depthRequired: Choose a Direct Superior depth from one to five.
v3.differentPeople: Choose different non-self employees, people and logins for the required approvals.
v3.superiorUnavailable: The superior is missing, inactive, ambiguous or part of a reporting cycle. Correct Personnel or explicitly offer an HR alternative.
v3.correctLevel: Correct this level and preview the assignment again.
v3.groupHrRefused: An HR alternative cannot complete a required selected-employee group.
v3.conversionHelp: This creates a new route draft starting with one level. The saved workflow and submitted applications keep their existing route until a new version is saved.
v3.calculationHandoff: This final decision needs scoped HR calculation access. Ask HR to record a reasoned reassignment of the outstanding participant; earlier approvals are retained.
v3.identityUnavailable: A required approver is inactive, has no unique usable login, or is outside the permitted company scope. Replace the selection or ask HR to correct their access.

v4.allRequiredHelp: Every listed person must approve; they may decide in any order.

aiManagement.title: AI management
aiManagement.description: See every AI capability, monitor model activity and control user and company allowances.
aiManagement.noProvider: No AI provider configured. Manual workflows remain available.
aiManagement.inventoryHelp: Pause or enable shared AI capabilities here. A ready capability still requires the caller’s normal permissions and available allowances. Readiness reminders can use a written template without a model.
aiManagement.scopedNotice: Shared feature switches are managed by a group administrator. You can edit allowances for companies you administer.
aiManagement.usage: {daily} requests today · {tokens} recorded tokens · {held} reserved tokens
aiManagement.noHistory: Activity starts when this monitoring is installed; older model calls are not backfilled.
aiManagement.reservationHelp: Reservations estimate capacity before calls. Recorded tokens include input, cached input and output reported by the provider. Missing usage or interrupted calls retain their reservation. Calls may finish above an allowance; further calls stop when recorded and reserved usage exhaust it.
aiManagement.limitHelp: Daily requests reset at midnight and monthly tokens on the first day of the month, Malaysia time. Each model exchange, draft or image read counts as one request, including failed attempts. Blocked calls do not consume the allowance. Blank means no additional cap; zero blocks new calls.
aiManagement.attribution: Shared calls count against every company in the caller’s authorized scope, including all companies for group administrators and organisation-wide scheduled agents. Both company and user caps apply; either can stop a call. Changing a cap preserves usage already recorded.

aiManagement.moreUsers: Showing the 50 highest-usage matches. Search to find another user.
aiManagement.noCompanies: No companies in your administrative scope.
aiManagement.businessLimits: Module access, feature permissions and the existing Performance limit of five successful drafts per field per user per day continue to apply.
aiManagement.legacyAssistant: Additional Assistant budget: {daily} questions per user per Malaysia day and {tokens} tokens per Malaysia month for the whole organisation. New questions count before a model call. Earlier monthly totals keep their original accounting period.
aiManagement.humanDecisions: AI remains advisory. Existing approvals and human decisions for pay, ratings, hiring and access remain required.
aiManagement.spendOptionalPolicy: USD caps are optional. Without an applicable cap, no USD ceiling is promised. Authorization and request, token, concurrency and time controls still apply. Any USD cap, including zero, requires verified monetary enforcement.
aiManagement.spendOptionalHelp: Blank removes only this field’s extra cap. Saving both fields blank explicitly clears this scope’s USD allocation. Other applicable caps remain; zero blocks new calls.
aiManagement.spendUnpricedUnknown: Calls with unknown, unpriced USD cost: {count}. These remain unknown and can block later USD caps pending review.

aiManagement.spendSemantics: Application inference allocation only. It excludes other uses of your key, credit purchase fees, taxes and provider billing differences. Unconfirmed charges remain reserved.
aiManagement.spendBreach: A confirmed charge exceeded its ceiling. Further strict admissions require review.

aiManagement.runsHelp: Latest 50 calls, including blocked and failed attempts. Metadata only; prompts, answers, images and credentials are excluded. Refresh to see new activity.

overtimePatterns.title: Overtime Patterns
overtimePatterns.descriptionText: Configure and review employee overtime, payable duration and payroll mapping.

overtimePatterns.empty: No overtime patterns match this scope and search.

overtimePatterns.unknownHelp: Unavailable historical facts remain Unknown. Current employee values cannot replace missing historical evidence.
overtimePatterns.unavailable: This pattern or version is unavailable in your current scope.
overtimePatterns.noChoices: No current authorized choices are available for this field. Validation will check recorded availability.
overtimePatterns.assignmentHelp: Individual assignments take precedence over group matches. Within the same type, higher integer priority wins; tied best matches are refused. End dates are exclusive.
overtimePatterns.formulaHelp: If no eligible-duration expression is configured, the supplied recorded raw candidate duration is used. It is worked duration before legacy overtime shaping; configure your eligibility and formula explicitly. Clock-dependent rules refuse missing interval evidence.
overtimePatterns.deductionHelp: Each canonical resource is deducted once per configured day or session. Overlapping rules cannot deduct the same source twice.
overtimePatterns.rateHelp: Higher priority selects the matching rate. Equal best matches refuse payment. Configure duration tiers and time bands explicitly; overnight bands must state the next-day boundary.
overtimePatterns.whole: One tier for the whole duration
overtimePatterns.mappingHelp: Map each tier to an authorized earning item. Actual transfer rechecks approval, payroll cycle, currency, source ownership and finalized payroll protection.
overtimePatterns.activationHelp: Save the draft, validate the saved revision, then activate with an explicit effective date. Stop and archive require a reason. Historical versions and finalized payroll remain protected.
overtimePatterns.saveBeforeAction: Save or discard definition changes before this action.

overtimePatterns.validationFailed: Correct the listed issues before activation.

costAllocations.instructions: How to fill in the Cost Center Allocations sheet. Company Code: the Company Code shown in People Management (where a company has no code yet, its registration number also works); the Allocation Reference sheet lists every company you may import for. Employee ID: the employee's ID in that company on the effective date. Effective Date: YYYY-MM-DD; the split applies from this date onwards and earlier history is kept. Operation: Replace on every row of a set, or Clear on one row with a blank Cost Center Code and Percentage to remove the whole set on that date. Cost Center Code: a code listed for that company on the Allocation Reference sheet. Percentage: greater than 0 and at most 100, with up to two decimal places; one employee's percentages on one date may not total more than 100 and may total less. Use one row per cost center. Rows with errors are not imported and each error names the row and the reason. No payroll values are changed.
